question.prompt:
A ship travels from point \(A\) to point \(B\) along a semicircular path, centered at Island \(X.\) Then it travels along a straight path from \(B\) to \(C.\) Which of these graphs best shows the ship’s distance from Island \(X\) as it moves along its course?

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Every point on the semicircular path is one radius from its center, Island \(X\). Therefore, while the ship travels from \(A\) to \(B\), its distance from \(X\) stays constant. The graph must begin with a horizontal part, which rules out A and C.

On the straight route \(BC\), the closest point to \(X\) is the foot of the perpendicular from \(X\) to that line. In the pictured route, this point lies between \(B\) and \(C\). The ship gets closer to \(X\) as it approaches this point, then farther away after passing it. The graph must therefore fall and then rise after its horizontal part. D instead rises and then falls, while E only rises.

These schematic graphs are compared by their changes in distance. The horizontal-then-fall-then-rise pattern gives choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Track the distance along each part
